result.summary: Reuses a single FuzzedWallet instance across iterations in the wallet fuzz harnesses instead of rebuilding it per input. A new test-only method CWallet::ClearInMemoryTxStateForTest resets transaction and coin-spend maps in memory without reimporting keys or touching descriptor state. FuzzedWallet now precomputes a destination pool, clears wallet transaction state per run, and periodically rebuilds the wallet after every 1000 iterations.
result.problem: Constructing FuzzedWallet for every fuzz iteration imports eight descriptors and incurs BIP32 derivations and multiple database transactions before reaching the target code, severely limiting fuzz execution throughput.
evidence: Author reports a ~6x speedup on an Ubuntu machine without sanitizers (PR description).
result.scope_notes: Adds a test-only method (ClearInMemoryTxStateForTest) directly to CWallet in production source files to allow harnesses to reset private in-memory transaction state.
result.changed_since_previous: Added a periodic rebuild every 1000 iterations to bound wallet state growth and an RAII drift check asserting bounded descriptor range movement during test execution.
result.card: This pull request optimizes wallet fuzzing by caching a single FuzzedWallet across inputs rather than reconstructing it every iteration. It adds a test-only CWallet::ClearInMemoryTxStateForTest method to wipe in-memory transaction and spend maps, while FuzzedWallet pools precomputed destinations and rebuilds every 1000 iterations. Rebuilding the wallet per input was paying descriptor imports and BIP32 derivation costs on every test run. The author benchmarks a roughly 6x speedup without sanitizers.

risk.why: ClearInMemoryTxStateForTest is test-only, so an error can only cause false positives or masked issues in fuzz testing rather than affecting production nodes.
